mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial register authority of the shareholder's home jurisdiction (e.g., UK Companies House, Delaware Division of Corporations)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; if the issuing state is not a party to the Hague Convention, full consular legalization through the Swiss embassy or consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Swiss Federal Criminal Records Office VOSTRA; for foreign residents, extract issued by the home jurisdiction's competent authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic certified extract by cantonal authority or Hague Apostille if issued abroad

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank confirmation of the blocked share capital deposit (CHF 50,000 minimum paid-up on CHF 100,000 subscribed capital) for the foundation deed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Swiss licensed bank (deposit-proof confirmation for the public notary)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Swiss bank-certified letter; no consular legalization required for domestic bank confirmations due to FINMA-regulated issuer status

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney for the Swiss registration agent or fiduciary, if founders do not appear in person before the notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notarial authority of the principal's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization depending on the issuing state, with certified German/English translation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP and sanctions screening of every UBO, founder, managing director and authorized signatory against the requirements of AMLO-FINMA and the Swiss GwG, covering the consolidation lists maintained by SECO (Swiss State Secretariat for Economic Affairs), the UN Security Council, the OFAC SDN list, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List and FINMA enforcement notes. Screening must include beneficial ownership transparency, adverse media, prior insolvency and politically exposed person status; any positive match triggers enhanced due diligence and, where suspicion arises, a report to the Money Laundering Reporting Office of Switzerland (MROS) within the statutory time frame. Foreign PEPs, their family members and close associates are subject to senior management approval under a documented risk-based assessment.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix (Central Business Name Index, www.zefix.ch) and the official Swiss Commercial Register electronic filing portal operated by the Cantonal Commercial Register Office of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug / iZug HR)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be registered in any of the official Swiss languages (German, French, Italian), in English, or in a combination thereof, provided the name is written in Latin script. Names originating from non-Latin scripts, including Chinese, Cyrillic or Arabic characters, must be transliterated into an approved Latin-script rendering; the applicant must provide a certified transliteration statement to the commercial registrar. All legal-form indicators (AG, SA, Ltd) are statutory; the chosen name must be clearly distinguishable within the same canton and not misleading as to the company's purpose, nationality or business scope, including compliance with the 'Swissness' regime for use of the word 'Swiss' or references to Switzerland.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Swiss / Suisse / Svizzera / Schweiz / Switzerland (ministerial approval of the Federal Department of Justice and Police required under the Swissness regulations)
Confederation / Federal / Government / Canton / State (implied state sponsorship; approval required)
Bank / Banking / Finance / Fund / Insurance / Assurance (FINMA licensing approval prerequisite)
Holding (only permissible where the company factually constitutes a holding company within the meaning of commercial register practice)
Group (requires substantive group structure and consolidated financial statements)
Trust (reserved for licensed fiduciary structures; prior cantonal commercial register approval)
Montreux / Olympic / Cross / Red Cross (protected identifiers subject to federal authorization)
CEO, FIA, GT, SRO or other terms falsely implying certification or regulatory recognition in the automotive sector
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon formal rejection by the Cantonal Commercial Register Office, the applicant may file a written administrative objection (Einspruch) with the same registry within 30 days of the negative decision, invoking Articles 14 and 27 of the Swiss Commercial Register Ordinance (ORC/HRegV). A further 30-day extension of the preliminary name reservation may be requested before expiration if no conflicting registration has intervened. If the registry maintains the refusal, the applicant may appeal to the competent cantonal supervisory authority for commercial registers (Aufsichtsbehörde über die Handelsregister) within 30 days of the definitive negative ruling, and ultimately to the Federal Administrative Court (Bundesverwaltungsgericht) in matters involving federal law. The payment of the administrative fee and submission of a legal opinion by a Swiss notary or attorney are generally required to accompany the appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Accepted with restrictions: Swiss company law requires that the registered office be located in Switzerland and correspond to the place where the company's actual administration is carried out (CO Articles 699 and 701). A purely virtual mailbox address is generally accepted by Swiss commercial registries for low-risk e-commerce entities where a registered agent, fiduciary or co-working provider maintains a physical presence, executive representation and service address in the canton. However, banks and payment processors (Stripe, PayPal) require documented commercial substance, including physical or co-working office evidence, business bank statements and tax/VAT identification; full virtual shell structures without any operational substance will fail the GwG 'economic background' due-diligence requirement and may be refused by the commercial register of Zug in practice.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Very low quantified baseline for a pure online aftermarket parts retailer without inventory in Switzerland: estimated 5-8% probability of an unannounced inspection or audit-visit per fiscal year. The likelihood rises to approximately 20-30% where the company later establishes a warehouse, stock-keeping unit or significant Swiss payroll, triggering routine cantonal tax controls and VAT field audits (MWST-Veranlagung) by the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV), since businesses with taxable turnover above CHF 100,000 are revenue-controlled every year; however, such controls are scheduled rather than spontaneous raids, and the Swiss criminal authorities conduct unannounced inspections only in cases of established tax or AML suspicion.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee of CHF 30 per extract for domestic certificates plus foreign extract handling

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht/OR), Articles 620–763 (Stock Corporation), particularly Art. 621 (minimum share capital), Art. 628 (organization of the board), and Art. 637 (registration)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Register of Canton Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Deed of Formation (Gründungsurkunde) and Application for Registration (Anmeldung) to the Commercial Register
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: AG requires minimum issued share capital of CHF 100,000; at least 20% of each share's par value must be paid up, in aggregate no less than CHF 50,000, and the paid-in amount must be held on a blocked Swiss bank account until registration (Blockierungsbestätigung).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: The First Board of Directors of [Company Name] AG hereby (1) acknowledges the subscription of share capital in the amount of CHF 100,000, represented by 1,000 registered shares of CHF 100 each, fully paid to a blocked Swiss bank escrow account; (2) adopts the registered office at [address], Zug, Switzerland; (3) appoints [Name] as Chief Executive Officer and [Name] as Chairman of the Board, each with sole signatory authority; and (4) authorizes the CEO to complete regulatory filings, open bank accounts, and execute contracts necessary to commence lawful operations. This resolution is effective immediately and shall be recorded in the official minutes. Unanimously approved by all board members on 1 January 2025.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarization of Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the German-language Articles of Association (Statuten) including the company name, registered office, purpose, share capital, board structure, and signatory rules. Arrange notarization of the Deed of Formation (Gründungsurkunde) before a Swiss notary, who will verify the legal capacity and identity of all founding shareholders and directors and attest the legal compliance of the founding documents.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or proof of registered office address
Written acceptances of directors and officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary issues a formal defect notice, correct the identified formalities and resubmit the revised deed for notarization within 10 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of Share Capital into Blocked Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a bank account in the company's provisional name and deposit the paid-up share capital (at least CHF 50,000 or the full CHF 100,000 if fully paid). The bank issues a blocking confirmation (Blockierungsbestätigung) confirming that the funds are available and will remain blocked until the Commercial Register issues the final registration certificate.
required_dossiers: Source of funds declaration for AML compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests further due diligence materials, provide source-of-funds documentation and economic substance information; restart the deposit instruction only after internal compliance approval.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application to the Commercial Register of Canton Zug
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register of Canton Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the formal application (Anmeldung) for entry into the Commercial Register, attaching the notarized deed, the bank blocking confirmation, and the signed declarations confirming that the founders and directors are eligible to serve. Upon successful review, the Register issues the legal entity extract confirming the incorporation of the Aktiengesellschaft.
required_dossiers: Passport copies of shareholders and directors
Signed authorization forms and consent to administrative procedures
Copy of lease agreement for registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commercial Register issues a material deficiency order (Bemängelung), cure the specified omissions or errors and refile within 10 business days to avoid an official refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) and UID Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA), VAT Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form 106 for VAT registration through the ESTV e-services portal and obtain the Federal Register of Commerce UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer) once the Commercial Register extract is issued. For an online retail operation with estimated annual turnover above CHF 100,000, VAT registration is mandatory. Simultaneously notify the Zug Cantonal Tax Office for corporate taxation.
required_dossiers: Statement of expected annual taxable turnover
Bank account details for tax refunds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax administration queries the turnover estimate or legal form classification, submit a revised turnover projection and audited supporting assumptions through the individual case contact within 10 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Social Security and Accident Insurance Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Compensation Office of Zug (Ausgleichskasse) and Swiss National Accident Insurance Fund (SUVA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company and its employees with the responsible AHV/IV/EO compensation office and contract with an accident insurance carrier under the Federal Accident Insurance Act (UVG). Submit the required AHV joining forms and declare employees for occupational pension fund (BVG) coverage, if applicable.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the compensation office requests missing payroll or employee information, provide the missing data within five working days; retroactive registration may be established by paying the outstanding social security contributions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Permit and Premises Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal Economic Development Office of Zug (Gemeinde Zug, Abteilung Wirtschaftsförderung)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the municipal business license (Handelsgewerbe-Bewilligung) under the Swiss freedom to conduct business. Submit the lease agreement, floor plans, and a fire safety declaration for the registered office and any storage area. This ensures compliance with local zoning, building, and fire-safety regulations for an online retail operation.
required_dossiers: Floor plan of the business premises
Fire safety self-declaration or certificate from the cantonal fire prevention authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If municipal authorities deny the permit due to zoning or safety objection, negotiate an alternative use or relocate to a compliant business premises; resubmit the application within 30 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable; no product-specific industrial license required for online retail of automotive replacement parts and tuning accessories under Swiss federal commercial law.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None – General municipal business permit only

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Category E (non-industrial activity, no mandatory EIA for warehousing and e-commerce distribution)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharge or atmospheric emissions; compliance with municipal wastewater regulations and Swiss Water Protection Ordinance (GSchV); waste disposal obligations under the Federal Ordinance on Waste Handling (VVEA) for packaging and returned products.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification required for the registered business premises under Zug cantonal fire protection regulations; basic occupational health and safety inspection under the Ordinance on Occupational Accident Prevention (VUV) after hiring employees; no structural load inspection required for office and storage usage.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung / Administration fédérale des contributions / Amministrazione federale delle contribuzioni) via the SuisseTax portal and eServices; cantonal tax administration of the registered seat for profit/capital tax compliance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the Aktiengesellschaft (AG) before a Swiss notary and register in the Swiss Commercial Register (Handelsregister), which triggers automatic issuance of the UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer / IDE / IDI); Step 2: For VAT, use the UID as VAT number once turnover exceeds CHF 100,000 or previously elected optional registration; Step 3: Foreign entities without a Swiss seat or permanent establishment must apply directly to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration for VAT registration using the official form for non-resident businesses, submit proof of foreign identification, appoint a Swiss VAT agent/representative for all service of documents and joint VAT liability unless exempt under special simplification, and receive a UID-MWST identification; Step 4: Complete additional cantonal registration for RHINO? no, for payroll withholding tax and social insurance if hiring Swiss staff; Step 5: No separate federal CIT registration number applies to the AG; tax returns are filed in the AG's canton of residence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; the AG is statutorily a stock corporation with separate legal personality and is resident for tax purposes when its registered office and/or actual central administration are in Switzerland; resident companies are subject to unlimited taxation of worldwide profits at the federal level (8.5% effective after federal tax) plus cantonal/communal profit taxes, while income from foreign permanent establishments and foreign real property is assigned to treaty-based territorial releases; capital tax applies at cantonal level; shareholder dividends are subject to 35% Swiss withholding tax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box classification regime exists; an AG is per se an entity-level taxed corporation. Swiss tax law provides for a tax group election for VAT (group registration) and a corporate income tax group (profit and capital tax allocation) when a parent holds at least 50% of the voting rights and operates a valid group structure under Swiss law. Hybrid mismatch rules follow BEPS recommendations but no direct tax-classification election is available for the AG itself; cantons may grant innovation-oriented 'deemed equity' notional interest relief, and the participation exemption can be claimed by holding and operating companies. Swiss entity classification for foreign shareholders follows Swiss domestic law and may be scrutinized under CFC/hybrid rules of the shareholder's jurisdiction.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Swiss Value Added Tax / Mehrwertsteuer / TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 of annual taxable turnover (exclusive of VAT) from supplies in Switzerland for Swiss-resident businesses; non-resident suppliers making taxable supplies in Switzerland also must register when Swiss turnover exceeds CHF 100,000, except for suppliers of electronic services to private Swiss consumers, where the same CHF 100,000 threshold applies but a simplified non-resident electronic services registration procedure exists; voluntary registration is available for non-residents without the threshold if the supplies are primarily in Switzerland and refund needs arise.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, electronic invoicing API, or digital stamping regime is currently in force in Switzerland; the QR-bill and eBill are interoperable private-sector electronic billing standards, not fiscal conveyor systems with mandatory tax authority validation. Every VAT invoice must contain the supplier's UID, the recipient's identification if the invoice exceeds CHF 300, the invoice date, the supply description, the consideration, and the applicable VAT rate or exemption reference. Auditable accounting systems under the Swiss Code of Obligations provide an audit trail, but there is no continuous transaction control pre-clearance obligation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods are zero-rated at 0% VAT when ownership transfers to a foreign purchaser and the goods are irrevocably exported from Switzerland to a foreign destination by the supplier, the foreign customer, or a third party on behalf of either; evidence must establish exportation. Services incidental to exported goods (including freight, storage, handling, customs clearance and quality inspection) may also be zero-rated. For online aftermarket retail of automotive parts or tuning accessories, margins and wrappers used in shipping, vouchers, and drop-shipping structures must be independently documented; domestic delivery to forwarding agents in Switzerland does not automatically qualify for zero rating unless a valid customs export declaration and transport evidence identify the consignee and destination abroad.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Swiss Customs Export Declaration (Autoeinfuhrzollanmeldung / export declaration opRIFN) with customs acceptance date and shipment reference
Origin copy or electronic equivalent of the bill of lading, air waybill, CMR consignment note, post/parcel declaration, or combined transport document evidencing exit from Switzerland
Commercial invoice with Incoterms, containing the full part number, quantity, sales value, currency, consignee and country of destination
Proof of dispatch from Swiss business records or the party arranging export, including warehouse release order or picking list

Inward remittance certificate or bank credit advice confirming the foreign customer's payment in the agreed foreign currency and account route (best practice; not a standalone Swiss statutory prerequisite)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Federal Tax Administration may retroactively reassess Swiss VAT at the standard 8.1% if the export substantiation bundle is incomplete, an unregistered agent intercepts the goods in Switzerland, or the sale is deemed to have occurred domestically; the taxable amount is subject to VAT plus default interest and, in bad-faith cases, surcharges up to four times the evaded tax under VAT criminal law. Fraudulent procurement of zero-rating, fictitious export declarations, or use of forged customs documents triggers criminal proceedings under Swiss customs and VAT provisions with monetary penalties, asset seizure, potential debarment from further export, and fines for individuals and directors. Audit scrutiny focuses on shipping timestamps, destination inconsistencies, cryptocurrency or IFZA? mismatches? payment mediation via Stripe/PayPal, and incomplete copy from remittance records; all documentation must be retained for at least 10 years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (Schweizerische Nationalbank), the independent central bank of Switzerland, responsible for monetary policy and the SIC/SIC+ payment rails, with concurrent AML/supervisory competence held by FINMA (Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority) over licensed banks and payment service providers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland provides unqualified current- and capital-account convertibility; CHF is fully freely floating and freely transferable with no exchange-control statute, no FX allocation system, and no restrictions on dividend distributions, loan repayments, or liquidation proceeds payable to foreign shareholders beyond the standard 35% Swiss anticipatory withholding tax, which may be reduced or reclaimed under treaty or statutory relief rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable: Swiss law imposes no mandatory repatriation timeline, no surrender/conversion ratio, and no FX requirement for export receipts. Exporters retain complete discretion over currency and bank placement; only statistical reporting of cross-border payments to the Swiss National Bank (payment statistics surveys) and universal anti-money-laundering documentation duties under the GwG apply.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: E-commerce settlement and SEPA rail account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium legal viability: foreign digital EMIs (e.g. UK/EU passport holders) cannot passport into Switzerland as credit institutions for CHF SIC settlement and may not hold funds for a Swiss AG without a FINMA banking licence, a Fintech licence under Art. 1b Banking Act (deposit cap CHF 100m), or a licence under the 2023 Payment Services Act. As a low-risk e-commerce merchant, CH AG may use a qualified EMI solely as an auxiliary collection/FX conversion rail for Stripe/PayPal receivables, provided gross settlement and liquidity buffers remain in Swiss domestic banks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: De facto required for at least one in-person KYC interview attended by the ultimate beneficial owner and a director at the Swiss bank's premises (or a FINMA-regulated co-operating intermediary); video identification is technically permitted under FINMA Circular 2023/1, but most prime Swiss banks require physical presence for non-EEA resident mandate signatories and non-resident controlled AGs before opening an operating or escrow account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: A newly incorporated AG with a high volume of Stripe/PayPal processor payouts and no audited financial track record
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified commercial register excerpt, UBO register extract, board resolution opening the accounts, 12-month auditable cash-flow projection, executed processor agreements and merchant statements, and a source-of-funds declaration approved by the board.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque shareholding chain or nominee share structure triggering GwG beneficial-ownership verification obligations
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current Aktienbuch (share register) excerpt signed by directors, the complete UBO chain of title to natural persons with passport copies, corporate charters of intermediate holding companies, and a FINMA Circular 2023/1-compliant beneficial ownership declaration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border supplier base involving CEE/APAC aftermarket parts with perceived third-party trade or dual pricing risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master supply agreements, Swiss customs e-dec declarations, HS 8708 tariff classification confirmations, transfer-pricing documentation evidencing the Arm's Length Principle, export-control certificates, and logistics contracts confirming the physical flow of goods.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Processor settlement mismatch or use of cascade payout accounts raised as unlicensed payment-services red flags
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Processor platform agreements, daily settlement reconciliation reports, and a legal memorandum confirming no provision of payment services to third parties; the account and cascade structure must be mapped and disclosed to the compliance officer in advance.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound paid-in capital shall be routed by SWIFT MT103 from the foreign shareholder's bank to the AG's Swiss beneficiary account referencing the corporate purpose as 'capital contribution (share subscription)'; the Swiss bank will require the board resolution, share-subscription evidence, stamp-duty evaluation under Art. 6 BStG (1% Emissionsabgabe only above the CHF 1m issuance threshold), and an explicit instruction distinguishing paid-in capital from shareholder loans, preventing misclassification that could trigger deemed interest or thin-capitalisation review. The beneficiary account must match the AG's legal name and IBAN exactly, and the originating bank must be screened for OFAC/Sanctions and FINMA intermediated-account eligibility.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: CHF/EUR outbound trade settlements use SIC/SIC+, euroSIC and SEPA CT for EEA suppliers; high-value non-EEA disbursements flow by SWIFT MT103 with trade-relevant Remittance Information (field 70) containing invoice number, purchase order number, and HS 8708 commodity description; documentary collections or commercial letters of credit (SWIFT MT700, UCP 600) are deployed for concentrated or credit-enhanced supplier relationships. Each wire is matched automatically against the underlying import invoice, customs value, and settled FX contract within the AG's treasury ERP to prevent duplicate payment and trade-based money-laundering flagging.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CHF/EUR forwards with a maturity of up to 12 months for purchase-side exposure
Deliverable CHF/USD forwards hedging Stripe/PayPal USD-denominated processor floats
ISDA 2002 cross-currency swaps (CHF/EUR, CHF/USD) for structural balance-sheet hedging

Restricted NDFs permitted only for genuinely non-convertible counterparty currencies when sourcing aftermarket components from restricted-deliverability jurisdictions and the trade risk is fully documented

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Combined federal and cantonal corporate income tax return with capital tax declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration at the registered office; Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) for federal direct tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the close of the business year; for calendar-year companies, by 30 June of the following year; extensions are commonly granted on request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest at the statutory default rate (approximately 3% p.a.); procedural fines up to several thousand CHF; default assessment by estimation; sustained non-filing may trigger enforcement and ultimately compulsory liquidation or deregistration from the commercial register

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Swiss VAT return and remittance of payable value added tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV), VAT Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the end of each VAT settlement period; default period is quarterly, with annual or semi-annual settlement available for approved small taxpayers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest at the default rate; procedural penalty up to CHF 5,000; additional fines for attempted evasion; ESTV may issue an estimated assessment and enforce collection

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (balance sheet, income statement, and annex) prepared and presented to the shareholders at the ordinary annual general meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders at the ordinary annual general meeting; the approved statements serve as the basis for tax assessments by the tax authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The ordinary annual general meeting must be held within 6 months after the end of the financial year; calendar-year companies must therefore convene by 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct administrative fine; an auditor's report, where required, must be presented; failure to hold the annual general meeting exposes the board to civil liability and may cause tax authorities to assess based on unaudited or incomplete figures

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Swiss Code of Obligations (art. 727 OR), an ordinary statutory audit is required if the company exceeds two of the following three thresholds in two consecutive financial years: total assets above CHF 20 million, turnover above CHF 40 million, annual average headcount above 250 FTE. A limited audit (review) is required when the company exceeds two of the following lower thresholds for two consecutive years: total assets above CHF 10 million, turnover above CHF 20 million, annual average headcount above 50 FTE. If neither threshold is exceeded for two consecutive years, the shareholders may unanimously dispense with any audit (opt-out under art. 727a OR).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations accounting and reporting provisions (OR 957-962), constituting Swiss GAAP. Listed companies must apply IFRS in consolidated financial statements; non-listed groups may choose Swiss GAAP FER, IFRS, or OR-standard accounting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Swiss law does not prescribe an annual UBO confirmation filing for a non-listed AG. Ownership changes must be reflected promptly in the shareholder register when registered shares are transferred; for bearer shares (still transitional in limited cases), the company must record the beneficial owner. AML-regulated financial intermediaries must maintain and refresh beneficial ownership documentation as part of ongoing client due diligence. There is no central public UBO registry and no annual confirmation to the commercial register.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 900 – USD 2,800 per year (typical CHF 800 – CHF 2,500) for registered office and corporate secretarial services in Switzerland
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 for micro-enterprises validly opting out of audit; USD 6,000 – USD 18,000 for a limited audit; USD 25,000 – USD 60,000 for an ordinary statutory audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal: 8.5%; cantonal and communal rates vary by principal seat; representative combined effective rate in Zug: 11.9%; national average: approximately 14.6%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays. Preferential regimes: patent/IP box deduction of 90% of qualifying net IP income (cantonal cap: 50% of taxable profit); R&D super deduction of 50% of qualifying R&D costs (optional by canton); participation relief for dividends and capital gains from qualifying shareholdings (85.5% federal exemption upon 10% shareholding or CHF 1.2 million market value); notional interest deduction on excess equity for qualifying financing operations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Combined federal and cantonal corporate tax return: 'Formulaire fiscal pour les personnes morales' / 'Steuererklärung juristische Personen'; electronic filing via the cantonal tax administration's eTax/ELMF portal (e.g., Zug: e-tax; Zurich: eFill; national ePortal).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; prepayments are quarterly; final self-assessment filed once per fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 6 months after financial year end; extension up to 4 months (total 10 months) for professionally accounted companies upon reasoned request; federal deadline follows the same rule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, registered office, UID/CH-ID, board members and authorised signatories; declare all corporate details as held in the Swiss commercial registry.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-owned AGs must state Swiss registered agent, principal Swiss office, and resident board member; absent Swiss substance may trigger anti-abuse scrutiny.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit before tax according to Swiss Code of Obligations annual financial statements; includes reserves and accruals, excluding hidden reserves.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Accounting must be prepared on Swiss principles; no attribution of group profit to Swiss permanent establishment unless actual functions/assets/risks lie in Switzerland.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible portion of dividend income, capital gains from sale of qualifying participations (shareholding >=10% or market value >=CHF 1.2 million); federal exemption rate 85.5% (100% exemption alphabet availability subject to cantonal rules).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign parent ownership of Swiss AG must be proven with share registry extract and TRC if dividend exemption is sought; tax ruling may be required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction of 90% of net income from Swiss or foreign qualifying patents/IP, limited to 50% of taxable profit at cantonal level; federal box is available with lower ratio.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: May only be claimed for Swiss PE that developed/patents or holds qualifying contractual IP; foreign owner must maintain economic substance in Switzerland.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Additional 50% deduction of R&D labour costs (Swiss activities; foreign research limited to 30% use), capped at 70% of employee contribution and 10% of cantonal profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If R&D is performed abroad for Swiss AG, claim requires actual Swiss R&D functions and staff; mere payment royalties to non-resident affiliate will be reviewed under TP rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report remaining deductible loss carryforward balances with year of origin; utilisation limited to 7 years forward, no carryback.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses follow the Swiss entity; a change of non-resident shareholder does not forfeit loss carryforwards unless restructuring is exclusively loss-saving with no business pursuit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Self-reconciliation of Swiss federal withholding tax (35%) owed on dividends distributed during the reporting period, including deemed distributions and hidden profit distributions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If Swiss AG distributes to non-resident shareholder, board must ensure 35% Verrechnungssteuer is withheld on time; otherwise personal liability attaches to directors.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Open-market value adjustments for cross-border intercompany transactions: inventory, royalties, management fees, financial dealings; attach contemporaneous local file and master file excerpts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders must supply benchmarking evidence and comparable data; FTA may either correct profit at Swiss level or reclassify payments as hidden equity distribution for WHT.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 301 (Federal Tax Base after Cantonal Deductions)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final taxable profit subject to Swiss federal corporate income tax at 8.5%; derived after amendments, participation deduction, IP box, R&D deduction, and loss carryforward offset.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-owned AG must confirm no profit allocation to foreign head office or associated supplier; standard independence requirement: arm's length pricing and substance documentation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing surcharge is up to 10% of assessed tax; procedural fines for non-compliance up to CHF 10,000; default interest on unpaid tax at 4% per annum; deliberate concealment attracts an evasion penalty of 33% to 50% of tax evaded, with imprisonment up to 5 years for serious tax fraud.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% gross Swiss federal withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer); refundable/reduced to treaty rate for foreign beneficial owners.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Foreign shareholder must submit the following to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV): Form 83 (refund application after dividend distribution) or Form 82E (advance relief before distribution); attach the Swiss dividend voucher, a current tax residency certificate (TRC) from the treaty country, declaration of beneficial ownership, and applicable domestic clearance under the Swiss DTA/Ordinance on Refund Speeding. Claim must be filed within 3 years from the end of the calendar year in which the dividend became due.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: generally no Swiss federal withholding tax on ordinary trade interest; statutory WHT applies only to interest on Swiss bank deposits and Swiss bonds. Royalties: no general Swiss WHT on licence fees paid to foreign payee if economically performed, safe from Swiss taxation absent a Swiss PE; DTA royalties usually remain taxable in the beneficiary's state at 0% to 10%, while excess royalties may be recharacterised as hidden dividend distribution subject to 35%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Swiss administrative practice expects contemporaneous Local File when cross-border intercompany transactions exceed CHF 1,000,000 in a fiscal year, intangible payments exceed CHF 250,000, related-party interest-bearing loans exceed CHF 5,000,000, or when transfer prices can be challenged by audit; a Master File is expected for groups with consolidated turnover above CHF 500,000,000; CbCR filing threshold follows OECD at EUR 750,000,000.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland has no EU-style Economic Substance Regulations, but federal anti-abuse doctrine and OECD BEPS require real entrepreneurial substance for treaty relief and corporate income tax treatment: a Swiss AG must have its registered office in Switzerland, a resident board, maintained books, active business premises, personnel who take board decisions, and bank account. Holding companies benefit form relief only if participation minimums are met and no artificial profit shifting; inadequate substance leads to denial of treaty benefits, hidden dividend recharacterisation and 35% WHT.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful submission of materially false or incomplete corporate tax return, understatement of turnover, overstatement of expenses, hidden transfer pricing margins, or failure to report a Swiss PE.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Evasion surcharge of 33% to 50% of evaded federal/cantonal tax plus default interest at 4% per annum; aggravated fraud using forged documents or sophisticated deception qualifies under Art. 186 DBG with imprisonment up to 5 years and criminal fine of up to 30% of evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Board members may be jointly and severally liable for civil restitution of evaded taxes if the AG is insolvent and directors breached prudence; travel bans, asset freezes and imprisonment up to 5 years for personal participation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Nominee board, no real office or phone, decisions made abroad, no substance for the auto-parts trading activity; misuse of Swiss legal entity to obtain DTA benefits or avoid sovereign enforcement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, mandatory tax reassessment under profit-adjustment provisions, cancellation of tax rulings; penalty up to 30% of underpaid tax and disgorgement refund of WHT; Swiss commercial registry may delete company for inactive shell status.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors/beneficial owners exposed to personal liability for unlawful wealth arrangement, asset tracing, cross-border claw-back actions, Interpol notices for money laundering, and exclusion from board functions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distribution of dividends to non-resident shareholders without collecting and remitting the 35% Swiss federal withholding tax; deemed hidden profit distribution of excessive royalties or management fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: FTA plus late interest; criminal offence of failing to withhold may be sanctioned with fine up to CHF 100,000 and full collection of underpaid WHT from company; qualified tax fraud triggers imprisonment up to 3 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable to the Swiss tax authorities for withheld but unremitted taxes and for the entire WHT debt if tax was intentionally avoided by decision of the board; criminal sanctions include imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the auto aftermarket e-commerce flow for third-party invoicing, payment passes through Stripe/PayPal with no traceability, trade-based money laundering via under-invoicing of car parts transactions, accepting proceeds from organised crime.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal proceedings under Swiss Penal Code (money laundering, Art. 305 bis: imprisonment up to 3 years, fine up to CHF 1,000,000); confiscation of illicit assets; permanent blacklisting from Swiss payment aggregators; civil fines for breach of AML gateway duties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individuals knowingly involved in the scheme may be prosecuted personally; travel bans, mutual legal assistance seizures, possible extradition; no corporate veil protection for criminal proceeds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False Transfer Pricing Documentation / Hidden Profit Shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing with fabricated intercompany invoices, zero documentation despite exceeding threshold, unreported cash flow to low-tax jurisdiction distributor, transfer of intangibles without arm's length consideration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Profit adjustment at full market value; penalty of 33% to 50% of additional tax caused; administrative fine for failure to submit documentation; conditional criminal prosecution if falsified documentation created by directors; cancellation of advantageous cantonal tax treatment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false declarations are personally liable in damages to the company for fiscal restitution and exposed to imprisonment for perjury-like false certification; court may order restitution plus 3 years imprisonment.
